description: Final proposed label set for intel/torch-xpu-ops (label-issue skill), organized by category. Includes proposed labels plus existing repo labels unchanged by this proposal.

issue_type_field.description: GitHub native issue 'Type' field values enabled in the intel org (distinct from labels). These are set on the issue Type field, not applied as labels. 'keywords' are heuristic hints used only when the native Type field is unset; they never override an explicitly set Type.

values.name: Feature
values.evidence: A request, idea, or new functionality

priority_field.description: intel org native 'Priority' issue field (org Settings -> Planning -> Issue fields) options. Set on the issue's native Priority field via setIssueFieldValue, NOT applied as a label and NOT a project field. 'tier' is the canonical name emitted in labels.md and is also the native option name; the 'option' P0-P3 values are legacy project names kept for reference only. 'keywords' are heuristic hints used only when Priority is unset; a human-set Priority is always preserved verbatim. See Step 3.4 (priority) of the label-issue skill for the full decision tree.

values.evidence: Any one holds: (1) a measured, quantified performance regression >7% between releases (a cited percentage, strictly >7%, not <=7%); (2) SIGSEGV/access violation on a Core API (import, tensor creation, .to(device)/.xpu(), matmul, .backward() on a <=3-op graph, nn.Linear/nn.Conv2d fwd/bwd, save/load, indexing/view/reshape); (3) a legacy Torch build failure (compilation/linker errors preventing a build).

Any one holds: (1) >6 distinct failed UT cases counted within the analyzed group (not the whole issue); (2) a regression citing a version where it passed and a current version where it fails; (3) a hang/timeout/deadlock (process alive but stuck, e.g. 300s timeout, infinite wait); (4) a benchmark accuracy regression that passed in a prior release and now fails without a crash (fail_accuracy). A performance regression is scored by percentage, not here; a benchmark accuracy regression outranks Medium functional error.

Any one holds: (1) a measured benchmark performance regression <=7%; (2) 1-6 failed UT cases counted within the analyzed group (not the whole issue); (3) a functional error without a crash (RuntimeError/AssertionError/incorrect result while the process continues); (4) a feature gap where tests fail because an API is NotImplementedError, without a crash. Default tier when no row in any tier matches.

Any one holds: (1) an enhancement/feature request (title asks to implement/enable/support/RFC/consider/investigate, or body describes desired new functionality -- but NotImplementedError is Medium, not this); (2) a validation or error-message difference vs CPU/CUDA without incorrect computation; (3) a minor/cosmetic/warning issue (warning mismatch, deprecated API, doc gap); (4) CUDA alignment where XPU behavior differs from CUDA but is not incorrect.

type.description: Issue type signal (labels). Native GitHub Type field values Bug/Feature/Task/Epic are NOT labels and are excluded.

labels.name: bug
labels.evidence: A reported defect/failure (type signal; mirrors native Type 'Bug')

labels.name: enhancement
labels.evidence: Request for new functionality (type signal; mirrors native Type 'Feature')

test.description: Which test surface failed. 'keywords' are the authoritative signal source for the extract_issue.md 'test' classifier; read them from here, do not hard-code them in the rule packs.

labels.name: test: ut
labels.evidence: Unit-test failure surface: a pytest invocation, a test/ path, an op_ut/op_extend CSV row, or a -k selector. Default surface when no e2e/oob signal fires.

labels.name: test: e2e
labels.evidence: End-to-end / benchmark failure surface (checked first): a benchmarks/dynamo|timm|huggingface|torchbench path or run_benchmark, or an authoritative-list model name together with a benchmark-context substring. A model name alone is not enough.

labels.name: test: oob
labels.evidence: Out-of-box model test surface (checked after e2e): an out-of-box/oob keyword hit when no e2e signal fired.

module.description: Code-category axis: exactly one label per issue. The label list below is ordered by decision priority -- when an issue matches several labels, walk this array top-to-bottom and take the FIRST whose evidence is met. The traced root cause is primary; 'keywords' are hints only. 'module: inductor' precedes 'module: dynamo' deliberately: every torch.compile failure walks through torch/_dynamo frames, so a Dynamo frame alone proves nothing -- choose 'module: dynamo' only when the defect is in tracing/guards with no backend-codegen signal. There is no generic 'module: others'; a failure that would fall through resolves to 'module: build', 'module: dpclang', 'module: rfc', 'module: utils', or 'module: infra' (the catch-all, last). 'module: ut' is NOT a member of this axis -- it is a test-surface signal on the 'test' axis. When judging by keyword, ignore the '## Versions' / 'Collecting environment' dump.

labels.name: module: distributed
labels.evidence: XCCL / ProcessGroup / DDP / FSDP / DTensor / symm_mem / collective ops

labels.name: module: sdpa
labels.evidence: SDPA / flash / efficient attention kernels (unless already claimed by distributed)

labels.name: module: profiler
labels.evidence: torch.profiler, Kineto, record_function, ITT, chrome traces

labels.name: module: inductor
labels.evidence: torch.compile backend: Triton codegen, lowering, codecache, AOTAutograd

labels.name: module: dynamo
labels.evidence: torch.compile frontend: graph breaks, guards, symbolic_convert, tracing (no backend-codegen signal)

labels.name: module: ops
labels.evidence: Other ATen/native ops: autograd, optimizer, torch.fx, torch.export resolving to an op

labels.name: module: core
labels.evidence: torch.xpu.* runtime, memory/OOM, RNG, streams, IPC, device management

labels.name: module: dpclang
labels.evidence: DPC++ compiler (dpclang) support surfacing during compile

labels.name: module: rfc
labels.evidence: RFC / design proposal / tracking-only feature request

labels.name: module: utils
labels.evidence: Torch utils not resolving to any op or runtime surface

labels.name: module: infra
labels.evidence: CI/CD, tracking, meta, test-harness -- the catch-all when no other module matches

labels.name: hw: PVC
labels.evidence: Ponte Vecchio / Data Center GPU Max

dependency.description: External dependency owner. A taxonomy value requires direct traceback/source/operator evidence that the failure originates in that component (see dependency.md and dependency_info.md); a library merely appearing in the call path never qualifies. This axis carries no 'keywords' by design -- unlike keyword-driven axes, it is evidence-only. 'code' is the bare taxonomy value the analysis resolves to; the emitted GitHub label is 'name'. 'exists_in_repo' defaults to true; when false the label must be created before applying and the reason must say so.

labels.name: dependency component: driver
labels.evidence: Failure originates in the GPU driver: a driver version gate, a submit/launch SYCL exception, or an explicit driver error. Not a library merely in the call path.

labels.name: dependency component: oneDNN
labels.evidence: Failure originates in a oneDNN primitive for an operator listed in dependency_info.md section 1.2: real-dtype matmul (Blas.cpp), convolution (Conv.cpp), fused linear (Linear.cpp), or quantized (qconv.cpp/qlinear.cpp). Listing alone is insufficient; the failure must originate in oneDNN.

labels.name: dependency component: oneMKL
labels.evidence: Failure originates in oneMKL for an operator listed in dependency_info.md section 1.1 with its stated Condition confirmed: complex-dtype matmul (BlasImpl.cpp), LU/triangular solve (BatchLinearAlgebra.cpp), or FFT (SpectralOps.cpp). Listing alone is insufficient.

labels.name: dependency component: oneAPI
labels.evidence: Host DPC++ / icpx build failure only (a build-time dependency, not a runtime one).

labels.name: dependency component: Triton
labels.evidence: XPU triton or libtriton, or an Inductor Triton crash. An eager (non-compiled) failure is NOT this value.

labels.name: dependency component: MSVC
labels.evidence: Windows C-runtime error (C#### code), cl.exe, or LINK.exe failure.

labels.name: dependency component: community
labels.evidence: A confirmed, relevant, OPEN pytorch/pytorch issue for the same failure.

labels.name: dependency component: third_party
labels.evidence: An originating non-torch site-packages/<pkg>/ frame (e.g. site-packages/transformers/). A site-packages/torch/ frame is PyTorch itself and is NOT this value.

labels.name: dependency component: oneCCL
labels.evidence: Failure originates in oneCCL: ProcessGroupXCCL, c10d, or a collective-op frame.

labels.name: dependency component: IGC
labels.evidence: JIT/IGC compilation, ocloc, shader dump, or an illegal-instruction failure originating in IGC.

labels.name: dependency component: Level_Zero
labels.evidence: A zeXxx call, Level Zero runtime, or device-enumeration failure.

labels.name: dependency component: PTI
labels.evidence: Failure originates in Intel PTI (Profiling Tools Interface): libpti/pti-sdk, ptiView* calls, or XPU profiler/Kineto tracing backed by PTI.

dtype.description: Data type involved in the failure. Multi-label. Emit a dtype label only when the dtype is part of the failure signature (failing test parametrization, error message, traceback, or reproduce command); a dtype named only incidentally does not qualify. Prefer structured fields first: the UT case name parametrization suffix, or extract.json E2E dtype; fall back to keyword matching. 'keywords' are the authoritative signal source; read them from here rather than hard-coding dtype spellings in the rule packs.

labels.name: dtype: amp_bf16
labels.evidence: Autocast/AMP bf16. Emit only when autocast/AMP is explicit; do not also emit dtype: bfloat16 unless the failure independently implicates the non-AMP dtype.

labels.name: dtype: amp_fp16
labels.evidence: Autocast/AMP fp16. Emit only when autocast/AMP is explicit; do not also emit dtype: float16 unless the failure independently implicates the non-AMP dtype.

triage.description: Duplicate / exclusion / split triage signals. 'keywords' supplement the duplicates.md and Step 2 grouping rules; they are hints, not a substitute for the two-of-three duplicate signal rule or the normalized-error-group analysis.

labels.name: duplicate
labels.evidence: An existing issue tracks the same failure: two of {same test case, same error message, same root cause} agree, OR a single verbatim full-test-name match in a skip-tracking body. A shared operator name or generic RuntimeError alone is never sufficient.

labels.name: wontfix
labels.evidence: Failure is out of scope / by design; skip the case. Set from the source issue own labels, or inherited from a HIGH/MEDIUM relevance duplicate carrying wontfix (absorbs legacy not_target).

labels.name: need_split
labels.evidence: The issue reports 2+ distinct failure groups (different normalized error signatures / root causes) that should be split into separate issues.

symptom.description: Failure-characteristic signals describing the nature of the failure. Multi-label: evaluate every label independently and emit one for EACH whose evidence/keywords are met -- a single issue routinely carries several (e.g. regression + inference, or Accuracy + training); never stop at the first match. An empty axis is valid. 'keywords' are the authoritative signal source for the symptom axis; read them from here rather than hard-coding them in the skill.

labels.name: functionality
labels.evidence: A functional failure: an operation errors, asserts, hangs, or otherwise behaves incorrectly (RuntimeError/AssertionError/exception/hang/timeout/NotImplementedError) where the defect is functional rather than specifically numerical accuracy, performance. Emit when the failure is a functional defect not already captured by a more specific symptom.

labels.name: regression
labels.evidence: A regression backed by an explicit before/after signal: a version or commit where it passed and one where it fails. The bare word regression in prose is not enough. A paired good/bad commit or version in the Versions block -- e.g. the '[Bug Skip]' CI template's 'latest good : <sha>' with 'current : <sha>' -- qualifies as this before/after signal.

labels.name: random
labels.evidence: A flaky/nondeterministic failure with an explicit intermittent signal (sometimes fails, not reproducible every time).

labels.name: inference
labels.evidence: Inference workload phase. For an E2E entry prefer extract.json E2E phase; otherwise judge from keywords.

labels.name: training
labels.evidence: Training workload phase (backward/gradient/optimizer step). For an E2E entry prefer extract.json E2E phase.

workflow.description: Existing status / triage / workflow labels unchanged by this proposal (not emitted by the label-issue skill).
